name: Replication Checklist
description: This module is a pre-completion checklist for replication work: a short set of checks to run before calling a replication task done.
content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for replication work: a short set of checks to run before calling a replication task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate replication outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. When multiple replication strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
3. Keep replication outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen replication approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. State assumptions about replication explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to replication (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Measure before optimizing any replication bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
8. Document any non-obvious replication decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting replication assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic replication advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop replication edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated replication concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of replication correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these replication guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
